raw_response:
Aiya, another season. It's just me and my old man on these 8 mu now — the kids moved to Handan years ago. Forty years I've been on this land, I know what it gives me.

The wheat is already in — I put it down back in October, same as always. Used the Jimai seed from the agri shop, same kind my neighbor Wang Sao uses. Before planting I spread 2 bags of the 15-15-15 compound per mu — that's what everyone around here does. When spring comes and the wheat turns green, I'll run the well pump for the returning-green water, then around jointing I'll topdress about half a bag of urea per mu. Some of the young ones put more fertilizer, but the bag of urea isn't cheap and I've been getting around 400 jin per mu for years doing it my way — no reason to change.

For water I go three times usually — returning-green, jointing, and grain-filling if May is dry. The well costs about 40 yuan per mu each time in electricity. If the rains come I'll skip the last one. One herbicide spray in early spring for the weeds — my back can't do hand-weeding anymore.

When the wheat's cut in June, I hire the combine from the village — 50 per mu, nothing to be done, we can't swing a scythe at our age. Then right away the maize goes in, we only have a few days. Old Zhang's son comes with the direct seeder, 40 per mu, drills it straight into the stubble. No plowing. That's how everyone does it now.

For maize I use the Denghai hybrid, about 80 per mu for seed. One bag of compound at planting, then some urea when it tassels. Maize doesn't drink as much as wheat here — usually the summer rains take care of it, I might water once in July if it's dry. Watch for the borer, spray once if I see holes. One herbicide spray too.

I reckon 400 jin of wheat and 450 jin of maize per mu. Same as last year. Not the best land in the village but steady. Good enough.
